fixes.title: Planetarium view hotkeys swallow typing in the search field - object search by name is unusable from the keyboard
fixes.summary: The screen wrapped everything in Focus(autofocus: true, onKeyEvent: _handleKeyEvent), which returned KeyEventResult.handled for bare c/e/f/g/h/m/n/r with no test for who owned the caret; a handled key never reaches the platform text-input path, so 'Vega' came out as 'Va' with the ecliptic and grid switched on. Replaced that Focus with a new SkyHotkeyScope widget that returns KeyEventResult.ignored for EVERY key while the primary focus sits inside an EditableText (walking up to EditableTextState, because a TextField's focus node belongs to the Focus that EditableText builds inside itself, not to the EditableText). The guard is unconditional rather than letter-only: a focused field also owns the arrows and +/-, which the sky binds to pan and zoom. Bigger than the finding implied: the scope also reclaims the keyboard on pointer-up when nothing owns the caret, because a field that loses focus to a tap on the sky hands it to the enclosing scope and left the whole screen deaf to shortcuts.
fixes.test: sky_hotkey_scope_test.dart (4 tests) in packages/skotiq_app: hotkeys fire when the sky owns the keyboard; they stand down for e/g/h while a TextField holds the caret AND the event still propagates to an outer Focus (proving `ignored`, which is what lets the character reach the IME); arrows likewise; tapping back onto the sky restores them.
fixes.caveats: Verified by reverting: with the guard and the reclaim removed, 3 of the 4 tests fail (the fourth is the baseline that must pass either way). The guard is a whole-key stand-down, so Escape no longer dismisses the object popup while the caret is in the search field - deliberate, a focused field is the one thing that should own Escape.

fixes.title: At a 1-degree imaging FOV the sky renders essentially empty - measured 1 star in 0.6 sq deg at astronomical dark
fixes.summary: Confirmed the cause independently from the installed catalog rather than from the app: hyg_v42.csv holds 119,626 rows, 41,149 at mag <= 8, 83,124 at <= 9, 107,938 at <= 10, 117,914 at <= 12 - the per-bin gain turns over after mag 9 (41,975 stars in 8-9, then 24,814 in 9-10, 7,580 in 10-11), so the catalog is complete to about 9 and the renderer is drawing what it owns. Two real defects follow and both are fixed. (1) kHygFaintFloorMag claimed 11.5, a magnitude HYG never reaches, and it was passed to the deep tier as minMagnitude - so an installed Tycho-2-depth tileset (complete to ~11) would have had almost all of its content discarded and the 9-to-11.5 hole would have survived the very install meant to fill it. Corrected to 9.0, and the seam is now max(kHygFaintFloorMag, manifest.magnitudeFloor) so a tileset's own bright cutoff is honoured instead of a constant overriding it. This also repairs the layers panel subtitle, which was telling users 'stars below mag 11.5 are unavailable'. (2) The silence: StarCatalogFallbackBanner fires only when HYG is absent entirely, so the common 'installed but far too shallow for this zoom' state showed an empty field and said nothing, which reads as bare sky rather than a catalog limit. Added starChartDepthLimitedProvider and a StarChartDepthNotice mounted in the shell that states the real depth at imaging-scale fields, with Install / Enable actions.
fixes.test: deep_star_hyg_seam_test.dart (3 tests) in packages/skotiq_planetarium - a recording DeepStarTileStore captures the seam the provider asks for and filters like the real store; star_chart_depth_notice_test.dart (5 tests) in packages/skotiq_app - the notice states 'magnitude 9.0' at FOV 1.2, is silent at FOV 40, offers Enable when a tileset is installed but off (and actually flips showDeepStarsProvider), is silent when the tier is on, and stands down for the louder no-catalog banner.
fixes.caveats: Verified by reverting the constant and the max(): 2 of the 3 seam tests fail, including the behavioural one where mag 9.5/10.4/11.2 stars vanish from the result. The depth-notice tests cover new surface, so 'fails without the fix' there means the widget did not exist. HONESTY POINT: this does NOT make a shipped user's 1-degree field deeper. No deep tileset is published (the settings card asks the user for their own self-hosted base URL), so mag ~9 remains a hard ceiling for anyone who has not built and hosted their own tiles. What is fixed is that the ceiling is now stated instead of being presented as sky, and that installing a tier will actually work when one exists. The Rust build_hyg_tiles binary the pack README points at is no longer in the repo.
fixes.needs_shared_change: To actually deepen the chart, someone who owns apps/desktop/assets/planetarium/** and the release pipeline needs to build and publish a Tycho-2-depth tileset (manifest.json + NSDT tiles) and point the default deep_stars source at it; packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/deep_star_catalog_card.dart then needs its 'no official tileset is published yet' copy and self-hosted-URL field replaced with a one-tap install. Separately, apps/desktop/assets/planetarium/catalogs/stars-hyg-v1 (768 NSPLNT01 tiles, 3.4 MB, still declared in apps/desktop/pubspec.yaml) appears to have no reader left in the Dart or Rust tree - worth confirming it is not dead weight in every bundle.

fixes.title: Object info popup keeps the old object's name and coordinates but recomputes Alt/Az for the NEW selection - it said Deneb was 'Below Horizon' while Deneb was 11.5 deg up
fixes.summary: The popup read its identity, catalogue coordinates and every action from the object captured at tap time, but read the horizon block from selectedObjectAltAzProvider, which follows the global selection. Bound the whole popup to its own object: alt/az is now computed from widget.coordinates with observerLocationProvider + observationMinuteProvider, so it still tracks the clock (scrubbing time and TONIGHT keep working) but can never describe a different object. That covers all THREE stale reads, including one the finding did not mention - the Log Observation dialog was recording the other object's altitude into a permanent observation record. The alt/az block is also no longer gated on there being a selection at all, since the popup always has coordinates. Second half of the fix, per the verifier: the popup now listens to selectedObjectProvider and dismisses itself when the selection moves off its object (by identity or id, so a search result rebuilding the same target does not close a correct popup), instead of leaving a stale card floating over the chart.
fixes.test: object_info_popup_identity_test.dart (3 tests) in packages/skotiq_app, at the live repro instant (2026-08-02 16:05 UTC, 40N/105W) with a star at +81 deg and M57 at -15 deg: the rendered altitude is the popup object's and the other object's altitude never appears; a selection change to a different object calls onDismiss; re-selecting the same target from another surface does not.
fixes.caveats: Verified by reverting both halves: all 3 tests fail. The popup now mounts the planetarium clock unconditionally, which starts observationTimeProvider's 1 s Timer.periodic - that tripped the pending-timer invariant in the existing planetarium_hud_labels_test, so its popup helper was given the same explicit teardown its bottom-info-bar helper already documents for exactly this reason (that existing test file was edited only for the teardown). Two suite-level failures are NOT mine: packages/skotiq_planetarium/test/benchmark/golden_compare_test.dart fails on all 5 checkpoints including wide-field ones the deep tier cannot touch (confirmed pre-existing by stashing my planetarium change and reproducing byte-identical failure numbers), and packages/skotiq_app/test/golden/public_screenshots_test.dart fails inside DashboardScreen with a SequenceLockedException before it ever reaches the planetarium capture.
